title: Varying flower longevity as a strategy to pollen limitation: implications for plant reproductive resilience under climate warming
screening_reason: Controlled pollination delay and final seed production directly quantify the cost of delayed pollen receipt but do not manipulate or estimate plant-partner phenological synchrony.
notes: Corydalis ambigua; 2024 experiment; Dryad 10.5061/dryad.wm37pvn3g. Valuable downstream mechanism/timing-sensitivity evidence. Do not count as an independent natural mismatch effect from the Corydalis long-term programme.

title: El efecto de Tegeticula yuccasella Riley sobre la fenologia reproductiva de Yucca filifera
screening_reason: Flowering/fruiting phenology and adult yucca-moth density were measured in the same year together with pollination efficiency and larval seed mortality; monthly synchrony-to-seed-output effect and variance still need full-text reconstruction.
notes: Yucca filifera × Tegeticula yuccasella; flowering Feb-May 1998, plant peak Mar-Apr, moth density peak Mar. Overall pollination efficiency 67% and larval seed mortality 3.8%. Strong mixed-system timing candidate but not yet a recoverable strict-H1 effect.

title: Co-pollinators and specialization in the pollinating seed-consumer mutualism between senita cacti and senita moths
screening_reason: Six-year flowering phenology and fruit-set experiments show timing-dependent access of diurnal co-pollinators while the pollinating seed-consuming senita moth remains temporally reliable; not a direct senita-moth synchrony gradient.
notes: Lophocereus schottii × Upiga virescens. Important H3 redundancy/timing-sensitivity context: late-season warm conditions close flowers before sunrise and remove bee contribution, but senita moth pollination remains dominant.
